A computed key is evaluated once at module load; `z.string().toString()` is not dynamic — it yields a fixed literal (likely '[object Object]'), so these are constant keys that will never match real fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`. Since the zod object strips unknown keys by default, safeParse returns only `access_token` (plus a `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` placeholder set right after). Callers in this diff confirm the impact: GoogleCalendarService uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then reads `token.expiry_date`, and Salesforce's schema requires `instance_url`, which the minimum schema drops when the sync env vars are set. So when credential-sharing is enabled, expiry/instance data is stripped and the per-app schema argument is ignored. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff; the affected path is gated behind env flags, so the severity is conditional, but the defect is real and introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In a JS object literal this evaluates once at module load to a single literal property name (a stringified Zod schema), not a “dynamic key”/pattern. As a result, the schema effectively requires an unlikely fixed property to exist and does not implement the intended “any numeric expiry field” or “allow other properties” behavior (Zod would need `.catchall(...)`/`.passthrough()`). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses this broken schema and ignores the caller-supplied `schema`, which can cause token refresh parsing to fail or drop required fields in the integrations updated to call `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (e.g., Office365/Zoom/Salesforce).
